name: Flood Tunnel Clearance
description: Session One's night quarter, and the campaign's first combat. Six Giant Centipedes, provoked by the party restarting a jammed drainage/compactor system they were sent to clear. Routine, sanctioned, paid by the head -- see ideas/story/bible/species/mitflits.md for why this is centipedes and not the mitflit nest the source material originally described. Runs the shared c1s1-compactor-cycle subsystem alongside it if that optional layer is in use.
environment: Cze & Peku's 'Trash Compactor' map. A single room: an elevated control platform to the north with the panels the party used to start the process, a step down to a large sunken central floor built around a glowing circular grate/compactor mechanism (flooded, murky, difficult terrain, poor light -- this is where the centipedes emerge from and where most of the fight happens), and conveyor-style walkways flanking both long walls, elevated and dry, giving a real tactical alternative to wading through the sludge. If the optional compactor-cycle subsystem is in play, the sunken floor also becomes actively dangerous ground as Encroachment rises -- the walkways are the reliable safe lane throughout.
specialRules: TRIGGER: the fight starts the moment the party gets the drainage system running (see the-basic-checks in episode-c1s1--flood-tunnel.json) -- the noise and disturbance wakes the nest. The centipedes are not surprised; treat this as a normal initiative roll for both sides, not a party ambush.

FOREKNOWLEDGE: if the party learned at Canteen that this wasn't just routine maintenance (c1s1-canteen.json's know-the-drains, ask-taka, or read-the-announcement checks), they enter already braced -- no mechanical bonus by default, just play them as prepared rather than blindsided. If a GM wants a real mechanical reward for investigating, the cleanest option is removing the centipedes' usual not-surprised status for that table only, letting an informed party roll for actual surprise -- optional, not the default.
OPTIONAL HAZARD: run alongside subsystems/c1s1-compactor-cycle.json for the 'closing in' version. The encounter and scene both work fine without it -- it's purely additive.

TONE, NOT SPOILER SPACE: what the party does to the centipedes (kill, drive off, or something else) is worth remembering for later continuity and for this specific party's own established character -- but centipedes are non-sentient animals with zero connection to the Observer/Watcher, so this is NOT the same thing as dossier-observer.md §13's Mirror mechanic. Don't conflate the two.
rewards: Standard combat XP for six level -1 creatures (20 each, 120 total) -- see reference/tables/encounter-and-rewards-math.json. No accomplishment XP; this is the routine job, not a triumph.
notes:
THE MATH. 120 XP for six creatures at party level -2 (20 each) is Moderate for a SIX-PC party, not the bare four-PC table's Severe -- per reference/tables/encounter-and-rewards-math.json's partySizeScaling (add characterAdjustment per PC beyond 4: Moderate's own adjustment is 20, so 80 + 2*20 = 120). ch1-v2.md's original 'Moderate, 120' label is correct once party size is accounted for; worth stating explicitly since the bare threshold table alone would misread it as Severe. Adding the optional complex hazard (c1s1-compactor-cycle, 20 XP at relative level -2 per the hazardXpByRelativeLevel table) brings the total to 140 -- still comfortably under six-PC Severe (180), landing as a meaningfully weightier Moderate rather than a dangerous fight. That's deliberate: this is level 1's very first combat and should stay firmly survivable even with the hazard running.

Giant Centipede's real stats (verified live against the Foundry 'Tales from the Vast' bestiary, 2026-09-09): HP 8, AC 15, Fort +7, Ref +6, Will +2, Mandibles (melee) with Giant Centipede Venom (Fortitude DC 14, Stage 1 1d4 poison, Stage 2 1d4 poison + Off-Guard). Full Strike bonus/damage, Speed, Perception and Stage 3 of the venom weren't captured in that pass -- pull them from the live Foundry actor at the table rather than treat any guess here as authoritative. No creature.schema.json file built yet for a portable stat block; a reasonable follow-up, not done here to avoid inventing numbers not actually confirmed.
